standard_prerequisites.name: Core and stable vertices
standard_prerequisites.statement: The core of a matching is the matching induced on its stable vertices and the two-row tableau T(m) records the unstable chords in its second row.
standard_prerequisites.use: They define the tableau whose descent set is computed.

standard_prerequisites.name: Short chord and descent set
standard_prerequisites.statement: A chord (i,i+1) is short when no vertex lies strictly between i and i+1, and the descent set of a tableau is the set of indices i with i+1 in the row below i.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the two sets that the proposition identifies.

standard_prerequisites.name: Stability of a chord intersecting a non-crossing chord
standard_prerequisites.statement: A chord that intersects another chord is stable.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the contradiction used in the proof of the reverse inclusion.

core_obligations: Show that the index of a short chord is a descent: the chord is unstable, so i lies in the first row and i+1 in the second row of T(m) (source line 902).
Conversely, take a descent i of T and use i+1 in the second row to produce an unstable chord (j,i+1) with j < i+1 (source line 904).

Rule out j < i by exhibiting an unstable chord (j,i+1) intersecting the chord (i,j') from the first row, which contradicts the stability of intersecting chords, and conclude (i,i+1) is a short chord of m (source line 905).

proof_roadmap.step: Short chords give descents, through the definition of the two-row tableau.
Descents give short chords, by an intersection argument that rules out an unstable chord starting before i.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled proposition at source lines 897-900: for a matching m in M_{N,f} with tableau T = T(m), the descent set of T equals the set of short chords of m. The proof (source lines 901-906) has two inclusions of different character: the first reads the descent directly off the definition of the two-row tableau, while the second takes a descent i, produces an unstable chord (j,i+1) from the second row and then has to exclude j < i by showing that the resulting unstable chord would intersect a chord of the first row, contradicting the stability of intersecting chords. The statement records the identity of the two sets and neither the construction of the unstable chord nor the crossing argument.
